adjudication_summary.description: Descriptive workflow statistic; NOT reported in the paper and NOT a post-adjudication agreement measurement. Each field counts round-0 disagreements between annotator A (Ginsberg) and annotator B (Moster) reconciled into the consensus by the two-round diff-and-revise protocol (which ended in a byte-identical SHA-256 endorsement). Units differ by tier and tier 1-3 are NESTED (tier N includes tier <N) -- DO NOT SUM. See iaa_report.json::_note.

tier1_disagreements_reconciled.description: Cluster-aligned code-point edit ops between the two round-0 tier-1 (consonantal) projections, over all verses. Reproducible from the two committed projections alone.

tier2_disagreements_reconciled.description: Same at tier 2 (+nikkud); INCLUDES the tier-1 consonantal edits -- not disjoint from tier1.

tier3_disagreements_reconciled.description: Same at tier 3 (full text); INCLUDES the tier-1 and tier-2 edits -- not disjoint.

tier4_disagreements_reconciled.description: Unmatched tier-4 detections (FP+FN) under the paper's §5.1 headline exact-match config (UXLC-anchored, canonicalised; 4 unalignable records dropped). Same frame as tier4.f1_mean.

cer_vs_consensus_b.description: ADJUDICATION DIAGNOSTIC, not an agreement figure. Annotator B's round-0 transcription vs the adjudicated consensus reference, per DRAFT_v4 §5.2. NOT a bidirectional A-vs-B agreement figure and NOT an independent human-vs-reference baseline: the consensus is A's round-1 revision, byte-identical to B's round-2 endorsement, so it is not independent of either annotator. For inter-annotator agreement cite cer_a_vs_b_round0. Renamed from bidirectional_cer_mean 2026-07-10 (B3).

ci95.description: 95% CI for cer_vs_consensus_b. Name kept for backward compatibility with benchmark-v0.1.0 consumers; the sibling blocks use explicit ci95_* names.

cer_vs_consensus_a.description: THE CIRCULARITY, QUANTIFIED. Annotator A's round-0 vs the adjudicated consensus. Near zero BY CONSTRUCTION -- the consensus is A's own round-1 revision -- so this measures how little A changed its mind during adjudication, not agreement with an independent reference. Published so the reader can see the circularity rather than infer it. Never cite as inter-annotator agreement.

cer_a_vs_b_round0.description: THE INTER-ANNOTATOR AGREEMENT FIGURE -- cite this one. Annotator A round-0 vs annotator B round-0: the only comparison here between two mutually independent, blind, PRE-adjudication transcriptions. DIRECTIONAL: annotator A is the reference/denominator; the B-as-reference direction differs slightly by denominator asymmetry and is given in iaa_report.json::_note. Its edit counts are identical to adjudication_summary tiers 1-3, which is the same measurement expressed as edit operations -- not independent corroboration.

denominator_codepoints_consensus.description: Consensus-side code points on this tier's view, over all 96 verses; the denominator for both cer_vs_consensus_* figures. Reference-dependent -- see denominator_codepoints_a.

denominator_codepoints_a.description: Annotator-A-side code points on this tier's view; the denominator for cer_a_vs_b_round0. Differs from the consensus side (one code point at tier 2, twelve at tier 3), which is why both are published.

edits_vs_consensus_b.description: Raw cluster-aligned code-point edit operations behind cer_vs_consensus_b.

edits_vs_consensus_a.description: Raw edit operations behind cer_vs_consensus_a. Published so a 0.0000 CER is legible as a real measurement (0 edits at tier 1) rather than an unpopulated field.

edits_a_vs_b_round0.description: Raw edit operations behind cer_a_vs_b_round0. Equals adjudication_summary.tierN_disagreements_reconciled by construction.
